source.title: Scaling Laws for Geospatial Foundation Models: A case study on PhilEO Bench
source.authors: Nikolaos Dionelis; Riccardo Musto; Jente Bosmans; Simone Sarti; Giancarlo Paoletti; Peter Naylor; Valerio Marsocci; Sébastien Lefèvre; Bertrand Le Saux; Nicolas Longépé

record.tranche_reason: The study varies geospatial model and pretraining-data scale and reports downstream task metrics, providing a conceptual test of downstream performance scaling. It does not measure language-model held-out cross-entropy or fit power laws.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern downstream RMSE and accuracy, not held-out pretraining loss. No power-law curves, exponents, small-run extrapolations, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations are fitted. The study also compares architectures and datasets; only results directly bearing on downstream performance versus model or pretraining-data scale are included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study varies model size and pretraining-data volume for Earth-observation image foundation models and reports downstream RMSE and accuracy. This bears loosely on V6 in a new setting. It fits no power laws and reports no pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. Its data-scale steps also change data composition: seasonal land-only, land-only multi-year, and global with ocean and ice. Tranche is T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors find no single best GFM: U-Nets (notably 200M on 2TB) excel in low-shot regression, ViT-UPerNet gains on segmentation at 23TB, and Mamba trades accuracy for efficiency. They also find that dataset curation (seasonal sampling, domain relevance) can matter as much as model or data size.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses satellite-image pretraining and downstream fine-tuning, and evaluates RMSE and accuracy on PhilEO Bench. It does not use language-model held-out cross-entropy, fit the original power laws, or optimize parameter/token allocations for a compute budget.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary by downstream task and data composition; the authors particularly note that GlobeEO's seasonal sampling benefits land-cover performance, while broader MajorTOM pretraining improves the reported road result.

fits_no_version.finding: Architecture family (CNN vs ViT vs Mamba) determines which model benefits from multi-terabyte pretraining; ViT gains on segmentation only at 23TB.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benefit of data scale for vision foundation models depends on architecture inductive bias.

record.problems: The evidence is downstream task performance, not pretraining loss or fitted scaling curves. Several comparisons change both architecture and dataset, and the text reports selected n-shot values rather than a predictive fit. No uncertainty estimates are given alongside the cited values; Table 3 notes best-performance selection considers ±3% variability.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss reported; no power-law fit in parameters, data or compute.
No controlled depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count; architecture families differ wholesale.
No power-law form fitted for image models; only three data scales and two U-Net sizes.
No predictive fit; no relation to pretraining loss; data scale is confounded with data composition.
No exponents or fitting choices compared.

missing.what: Table 3 averaged limited/large n-shot metrics for 44M-0.5T, 44M-2T, 44M-23T, 200M-2T and ViT 100M-2T/23T. At large n-shot, building RMSE worsens with more data (0.059→0.061→0.063), and 200M-2T is listed worse than 44M-2T. These are mixed or non-monotonic trends, with a possible label swap.
Gains from 23TB pretraining appear mainly below 500 shots and diminish as labelled samples increase.
Scaling the U-Net 44M→200M raises FLOPs 5.87G→82.23G while RMSE improves only modestly.

record.verdict_notes: Non-LLM Earth-observation vision study; its link to V6 (stated for LM scaling) is loose. Data-scale steps change data distribution, so they are not clean scale tests. Table 3 FLOPs suggest the 44M-2T and 200M-2T rows may be mislabelled.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits to small runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its scaling with compute.
Controlled comparisons of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether a power-law form holds for image or other modalities, or under repeated-data, fine-tuning, and transfer regimes.
No predictive fit or relationship to pretraining loss is tested; the study reports selected downstream outcomes across model/data scales rather than a general predictive law.
No exponents or compute-optimal split are fitted or compared across fitting choices.

rows.subject: Geo-Aware U-Net 200M-2T
rows.operation_detail: Compared model parameter scale at fixed 2TB pretraining data.
rows.note: The text reports this as a model-size comparison at the same pretraining-data scale.
rows.check: Single hand-picked point (building, n=50). Table 3 averages conflict: 200M-2T is worse than 44M-2T on all six averaged metrics. The 44M-2T and 200M-2T FLOPs entries look swapped, since the text says 44M→200M goes 5.87G→82.23G, so the table labels may be swapped too.

rows.subject: Geo-Aware U-Net 44M-2T
rows.operation_detail: Compared pretraining-data scale for the same 44M model.
rows.baseline: 0.62 for Geo-Aware U-Net 44M pretrained on GlobeEO 0.5TB
rows.note: The authors attribute the advantage of GlobeEO here to its four-season sampling.
rows.check: More data (0.5TB→2TB) also changes composition, from seasonal 4x/year to random decade time steps. The authors attribute the drop to the loss of seasonal sampling, not to scale.

rows.subject: ViT UPerNet 100M-23T
rows.operation_detail: Compared a large-scale pretraining run with the smaller seasonal GlobeEO reference.
rows.note: The comparison changes both architecture and pretraining dataset.
rows.check: Compares ViT-UPerNet 100M on 23TB with U-Net 44M on 0.5TB. Architecture, size and data all change, so this is not a scale comparison of one model.

rows.subject: Geo-Aware U-Net 44M-23T
rows.operation_detail: Compared a large-scale pretraining run with the smaller seasonal GlobeEO reference.
rows.note: The text says both 23TB models fall below the 0.5TB seasonal-data result.
rows.check: Same 44M U-Net, 0.5TB→23TB, accuracy 0.62→0.54. Confounded by composition change: ocean/ice added and seasonal sampling lost.

rows.subject: Geo-Aware U-Net 44M-23T
rows.operation_detail: Compared pretraining-data scale for the same model.
rows.baseline: 0.071 for the same model pretrained on GlobeEO 0.5TB
rows.note: The text describes this as a 5.6% improvement.
rows.check: Modest 5.6% gain at a single n-shot. Data composition also changes.

relationships.condition: Geo-Aware U-Net, regression tasks at low shots (building n=50, 44M→200M at 2TB; road n=100, 0.5TB→23TB)
relationships.reason: Larger model or more pretraining data lowers RMSE by 22% (R1) and 5.6% (R5). These are isolated selected points.
relationships.display_finding: Scaling the model reduced building-regression RMSE by 22%, while increasing pretraining data reduced road-regression RMSE by 5.6% in selected comparisons.

relationships.condition: Land cover segmentation at n=100, Geo-Aware U-Net 44M, larger but differently composed pretraining data (2TB, 23TB vs seasonal 0.5TB)
relationships.reason: Accuracy drops from 0.62 to 0.58 (R2) and to 0.54 (R4) as data grows. The authors attribute this to composition (seasonal sampling), so gains depend on task and data curation.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy fell from 0.62 with seasonal 0.5TB data to 0.58 with 2TB and 0.54 with 23TB, which the authors attributed to data composition.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Building density at 50 shots with Geo-Aware U-Net models pretrained on FastTOM 2TB; road density at 100 shots with Geo-Aware U-Net 44M pretrained on 0.5TB versus 23TB
reader_labels.reason: The larger model at fixed data scale has lower RMSE, and the 23TB pretraining run has lower road RMSE than the 0.5TB run (R1, R5).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Land cover mapping at 100 shots, comparing GlobeEO 0.5TB with the stated 2TB or 23TB runs
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy is lower for the larger-data runs in these reported comparisons, rather than improving uniformly with pretraining scale (R2, R3, R4).
